items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The line-up was Jimmy Archey, trombone, Henry 'Moon' Jones had replaced Charlie Holmes on alto sax... and myself, trumpets.

ctx.x: As for socializing with the clientele was concerned, no band, white or coloured, was allowed to do that. And everyone, clients, musicians, bartenders and hostesses came in and went out the front door. We came and left by a back door at the Roseland.

Russel was now employing three trumpets and Higginbotham was not there. The line-up was Jimmy Archey, trombone, Henry 'Moon' Jones had replaced Charlie Holmes on alto sax, Greely Walton had replaced Teddy Hill on tenor-sax, Albert Nicholas, alto-sax and clarinet, Bill Johnson, guitar, Paul Barbarin, drums, Pops Foster, bass, Bill Dillard, Red Allen and myself, trumpets. And this time I had more solos and played some of the first parts also.

One night the orchestra of Noble Sissle who was working in a big white hotel was engaged at the Arcadia to play a battle of jazz between Russell and the other white orchestra whose name I don't remember. I had seen Sissle on stage when I was in Cincinnati and in my estimation he was pretty much a ham actor. So it was a night that we were looking forward to, and the Uncle Tom in him was really shown when his band came in dressed in red frocktail coats which made them look like a circus monkey band.
